## Verdict
Needs work. Every hard mandate filter passes. The deal fails three soft tests: going-in net yield on total cost is 5.83% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] against a 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum, levered IRR is 1.86% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] against 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]], and the equity multiple is 1.09x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] against 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]].

Recommendation: do not commit diligence spend at the asking price of AED 113.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. Re-engage only at or below AED 97.17m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], which is 14.01% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] under asking and is set by the levered IRR target.

## The deal
- Larkspur Residence, Barsha Heights (TECOM), Al Barsha. 126 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2011 [[deal.completion_year]], freehold, single title.
- Asking AED 113.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], AED 911 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] on NSA, per the OM.
- Direct leases, no master tenant. In-place rent is AED 10.08m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] with 95.24% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy (6 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]]). The landlord pays chiller costs; district cooling is AED 1.03m [[opex.district_cooling]] a year.

The OM headlines 5.97% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI over price plus acquisition costs) it is 5.83% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]], a gap of -0.14% [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]]. The OM figure takes passing rent with no vacancy or collection-loss deduction.

## What would make it fail
- **Exit pricing.** Even the base case loses money on the sale. Gross exit value at a 7.00% [[uw.exit_yield]] exit yield is AED 109.09m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], and the levered exit result is AED -13.12m [[uw.exit_gain_levered_aed]]. With the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, levered IRR is -0.26% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. The best grid case, market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, reaches only 6.53% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]], still short of 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]].
- **Rent softness.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower, levered IRR is -0.85% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.levered_irr_pre_tax]], and -3.06% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]] with the exit yield also 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider. The market rent reference for Al Barsha is unverified.
- **The upside story is not there.** The OM claims about 13% [[om.upside_claim_2]] from re-basing rents at renewal. Under the RERA rent-increase bands no lease expiring in the next two years can rise by more than 10.0% [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.why]], and renewals move rent 0.5% [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.why]] on average. Units let above market, 9.43% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of income, reset down.
- **Near-term rollover.** The largest expiry window, between 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 29 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]], holds AED 3.00m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent, 29.77% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of the total. That is inside the 40.00% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]] limit but lands on a falling-rent assumption.

Debt is not the weak point: DSCR holds at 1.43x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.dscr_year1]] in the weakest rent case.

## Discrepancies that matter
1. **High: claimed rent uplift.** The OM says re-basing at renewal adds about 13% [[om.upside_claim_2]]. The screen relied on its own unit-by-unit RERA band rule, which caps increases at 10.0% [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.why]] and gives an average renewal move of 0.5% [[disc.upside_exceeds_rera_cap.why]]. We give the claimed reversion no value, so the OM's upside is absent from our returns.
2. **Medium: partial-year operating statement.** The statement covers 9 months [[opex.months]] and the seller annualised it. One-off and seasonal costs such as insurance renewals and annual maintenance contracts may be misstated, and recent changes are hidden. The screen relied on the statement and then applied its own cost assumptions, so Year-1 operating costs are AED 3.28m [[uw.operating_costs_year1]] against the seller's AED 3.02m [[opex.total_expenses_aed]].

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- Broker's list of units behind the reversion claim, each tested against the RERA calculator.
- Full year of monthly operating statements and the general ledger for one-off items.
- Rent roll with arrears, notice and renewal status, plus a full year of collections data.
- Independent verification of the Al Barsha market rent reference.
- Transfer of security deposits to the buyer at closing.

## Assumptions
Debt is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] loan to value at 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]] (3M EIBOR 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] plus 2.50% [[assume.margin]] margin), amortising over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. Underwriting uses 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] structural vacancy, 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]] collection loss and a 5.00% [[assume.management_fee]] management fee. Market rent moves -4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. The exit yield is 7.00% [[uw.exit_yield]] after 5 years [[uw.hold_years]], with analysis starting 1 January 2027 [[uw.analysis_start]]. No operating cost categories were filled from defaults.
